[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
Daniel Glasco/Glascow, Norfolk planter, conveys 100 acres to Richard Linton with the consent of Mary, explicitly his wife, from Henry Slade’s 330-acre patent. The deed was recorded on 3 September 1729; the upper endorsement expressly says Daniel came into court and acknowledged it, proving him alive on that date.<ref>Princess Anne County, Deeds and Wills Book4 Part1 (1724–1735), manuscript p.207, DGS7645780; https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-99PX-F3DX. Original deed-book image partly read at limited resolution. Exact execution dates and the earlier William title recital remain provisional. No father clause was inspected; Daniel’s identity remains unresolved. William Glasgow-428 is not named; the linked profile preserves the associated property-trail research.</ref>

Daneill Glasco witnesses Richard Johnson’s Norfolk will dated 26 February 1729/30, with Richard Linton and John Moy. The will was proved on 18 September 1730.<ref>Unidentified Daneill Glasco witnesses a Norfolk will; https://www.familysearch.org/library/books/viewer/166084/. McIntosh, printed p.122 (not112), visually inspected; not the original will manuscript. The witness’s identity with either Daniel profile is unresolved. No father or survival-to-probate inference. William Glasgow-428 is an associated research case and is not named in this entry.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The 1729 planter and 1729/30 witness are compatible with one man; shared Richard Linton supports the cluster. Daniel Glasgow-3322, husband of Mary Gamon in 1693, remains a candidate: his before 1675 birth and missing death do not exclude 1729. No land-title bridge yet proves continuity.
Possible identities: [[Glasgow-3322|Glasgow-3322]]. These are possible candidates, not established matches.
Next identity test: Compare the cited originals with the linked candidate biographies and seek a matching family, address, age or property chain.

It is a useful later locality lead because Lisnagaver is the Glasgow family's documented townland and the directory places a McCaughern farmer there after the 1851 and 1901–1911 census evidence.<ref>1912 Belfast and Ulster Directory, Rasharkin; https://lennonwylie.co.uk/PT191214.htm; . It does not identify Robert's age, parents or relationship to Mary Glasgow, and it must not be merged with any other Robert McCaughern without the underlying valuation, census or civil records.</ref>

The original 1911 Lisnagaver return identifies Robert McCaughern, 54, farmer, with wife Mary Anne, 58; married 28 years, both Antrim-born Church of Ireland. The occupation and exact locality strongly identify the 1912 directory farmer. His parents are not stated.<ref>1911 Lisnagaver, Robert McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001389352.pdf; Form A; official index house 2; printed number altered; rows 1–2. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

Mary Anne may be compared with McCaughern-24, but age and name alone neither identify nor exclude her.

Possible profile identities: none established within the recorded searches.

== Biography ==

The published headstone transcription for Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church records a memorial erected by Alexander Elder of Gortrickey to his father Robert Elder, his mother Jane, and his sisters and brothers. It also records Alexander Elder's death on 5 January 1943.<ref>Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church headstones; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/graveyard.html; . This is a new direct memorial transcription for the catalogue's parentage study, not a Glasgow record and not proof that the Elder family was related to Alexander Glasgow. Its value is locality context: Gortrickey/Gortereghy is the townland where the Glasgow family appears in the 1837–1838 Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism entries. The memorial supplies a named Elder household for future comparison with the later Robert Elder who occupied Alexander Glasgow's former Lisnagaver lot; identity between those Elder references remains unproved.</ref>

The same reproduced Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records Neal Anderson, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, marrying Sarah Elder, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, on 28 September 1893. Sarah's father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Nancy Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . This is a new parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and is consistent with the 1908 entry naming Alexander Elder as a son of a Robert Elder, but the shared father's identity and any connection to Robert Elder, husband of Mary Glasgow, remain unproved until the original register is inspected.</ref>

The reproduced Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records Isaac Elder, full-age bachelor farmer of Gohorney, marrying Jane Elliott on 19 February 1903. Isaac's father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . This is another catalogue-absent parent-bearing record for a Robert Elder household in the Rasharkin area. It supports the existence of a substantial local Elder family network, but does not by itself identify Isaac's Robert with Robert Elder, husband of Mary Glasgow, or establish any Glasgow relationship.</ref>

A 2007 RootsChat research post reproduces a 18 June 1908 Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage entry for Alexander Elder, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, whose father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer. Alexander married Mary Anderson, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, daughter of Neil Anderson; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Margaret Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . The entry is not yet an inspected original, so it is a secondary-source lead rather than final evidence. It is nevertheless a new, specific parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and gives a testable route for determining whether the Alexander Elder on the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial was a son of the Robert Elder who later occupied Alexander Glasgow's Lisnagaver lot. That identity chain remains unproved.</ref>

The original 1901 Gortereghy return records Robert Elder, 65, widowed farmer, with Alex 27 and Robert 20 as sons and Eliza 22 and Margaretta 14 as daughters. The 1911 Alexander/Mary household explicitly records Robert as Alexander’s brother and Margaret as his sister. The combined names and locality strongly support continuity, with age differences retained. Robert Elder-7144 remains a qualified father identity; Robert/Mary Glasgow’s Gortahar household is separate.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Robert Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298460.pdf; Form A; official index house 42; rows 1–5; 1911 Gortereghy, Alexander Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390156.pdf; Form A; official index house 37; rows 1–4. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

The original birth entry names Jane Elder, born 27 April 1881 at Gortreighy, daughter of farmer Robert Elder and Jane formerly Calderwood. This identifies that parental couple and strengthens the separate Robert/Jane study; it does not yet prove Jane Calderwood as mother of all 1901/1911 siblings.<ref>Ballymoney civil birth register 1881; https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1881/02832/2038201.pdf; printed page 166; PDF page 1; entry 279. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Elder-7144 remains compatible for the living 1901 father of Alex/Robert/Eliza/Margaretta; its 1827 birth is tree-derived and differs from reported age 65, so retain uncertainty. Elder-7251 represents Mary Glasgow’s separate Gortahar family: she is a widow there in 1901 while the Gortereghy Robert is alive. Do not exclude Elder-7251 globally from Sarah’s 1893 father clause merely because a father can be deceased at marriage. Sarah and Isaac’s father occurrences remain unproved bridges to the 1901 family. The original 1881 Jane birth proves Robert/Jane Calderwood as a parental couple, not the mother identity of all later siblings.

This is a new direct memorial transcription for the catalogue's parentage study, not a Glasgow record and not proof that the Elder family was related to Alexander Glasgow. Its value is locality context: Gortrickey/Gortereghy is the townland where the Glasgow family appears in the 1837–1838 Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism entries. The memorial supplies a named Elder household for future comparison with the later Robert Elder who occupied Alexander Glasgow's former Lisnagaver lot; identity between those Elder references remains unproved.</ref>

A 2007 RootsChat research post reproduces a 18 June 1908 Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage entry for Alexander Elder, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, whose father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer. Alexander married Mary Anderson, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, daughter of Neil Anderson; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Margaret Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . The entry is not yet an inspected original, so it is a secondary-source lead rather than final evidence. It is nevertheless a new, specific parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and gives a testable route for determining whether the Alexander Elder on the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial was a son of the Robert Elder who later occupied Alexander Glasgow's Lisnagaver lot. That identity chain remains unproved.</ref>

The inspected original 1911 Gortereghy census return records Alexander Elder, aged 40, as head, Mary Elder, aged 44, as wife, Robert Elder, aged 34, as brother, and Margaret Elder, aged 25, as sister (Form A, official index house 37, nai001390156, rows 1–4). These stated relationships support comparison with the 1901 household, the 1908 marriage lead and the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial; identification with existing profiles remains qualified.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Alexander Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390156.pdf; Form A; official index house 37; rows 1–4. Original register or Form A inspected on 30 September 2026; source-specific image and entry references supplied. Profile identities and cross-record continuity remain qualified where stated.</ref>

The original 1901 Gortereghy return records Robert Elder, 65, widowed farmer, with Alex 27 and Robert 20 as sons and Eliza 22 and Margaretta 14 as daughters. The 1911 Alexander/Mary household explicitly records Robert as Alexander’s brother and Margaret as his sister. The combined names and locality strongly support continuity, with age differences retained. Robert Elder-7144 remains a qualified father identity; Robert/Mary Glasgow’s Gortahar household is separate.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Robert Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298460.pdf; Form A; official index house 42; rows 1–5; 1911 Gortereghy, Alexander Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390156.pdf; Form A; official index house 37; rows 1–4. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

The original 1901 Alex is explicitly Robert’s son; the 1911 return names brother Robert and sister Margaret. Together with the 1908 Alexander/Mary Anderson marriage extract, these support one sibling family. Retain the actual age differences. Use the same qualified Elder-7144 father hypothesis for Alexander and proved siblings; mother Jane on the memorial is separately evidenced, while Jane Calderwood remains a comparison. No matching Alexander profile was established in full same-name and father-filtered searches.

Possible profile identities: none established within the recorded searches.

== Biography ==

The source previously cited for a supposed 8 November 1839 Kilraughts marriage was rechecked. Its entry is for Alexander Montgomery, a shoemaker, marrying Jane McCaughey, daughter of John McCaughey, before witnesses Betty Hay and William Hay.<ref>Ulster Lees, Ballymoney area research, entry for Alexander Montgomery and Jane McCaughey; https://ulsterlees.azurewebsites.net/families/co-antrim/ballymoney-area/; ; Churchtown Presbyterian baptisms; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/TamlaghtP/Baptisms.html; . It does not name Alexander Glasgow, Mary McCaughan/McAughin, or any Glasgow parent.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Hay-867 represents William of Carrickfergus/Irish Quarter, born about 1808 and married to Elizabeth Walker in 1829. His age is compatible with witness William Hay at Kilraughts in 1839. A different earlier residence and absence of a witness connection do not exclude him. This remains a weak candidate, not proof.

Possible profile identities: [[Hay-867]].

people.wikitext:
== Biography ==
David Mathy and Mergaret Androsoune, expressly his spouse, bought a barn at Powdrait, Glasgow, from John Hawstoune on 3 February 1550/51. The property adjoined Peter Adam’s land west, James Hyndschaw’s east, the street north, and Malindin or burn south.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol.1, protocol71, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsofproto01glas/page/n60/mode/1up p.27]; page image inspected 30 September 2026.</ref>

A David Mathy was expressly a fellow Glasgow burgess with Robert Glesgw among witnesses to John Androsoune’s sasine on 10 May 1554. The same-day act in protocol184 had the same witnesses.<ref>Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol.1, protocols183–184, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsofproto01glas/page/n96/mode/1up p.63]; page image inspected 30 September 2026.</ref> David also witnessed a transaction on 4 July 1554.<ref>Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol.1, protocol189, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsofproto01glas/page/n98/mode/1up p.65]; page image inspected 30 September 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The purchaser and later witness are probably the same man by name and Glasgow property/civic context, but the 1554 acts do not name his wife. No inspected entry calls him kin of Robert Glesgw or names his parents. The 1550/51 transaction proves the documentary marriage, not an existing profile identity for either spouse. Margaret Anderson-3241 is a sparse compatible spouse candidate, with unknown dates and unsupported family; identity remains unresolved. The companion subject draft records her separately with the same qualification. [[Matthew-330|David Matthew]] remains a weak compatible variant candidate because its 1701 death is an unsupported GEDCOM field; do not exclude it or create another David solely from that field.

== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' appears in a shipping report headed ''Greenock, August 12'', published on 18 August 1740. The arrival list reads: “The Prosperity of Irvine, James Glasgow, from Northcopen.”<ref>''The Caledonian Mercury'', 18 August 1740, page 3, Greenock shipping list. [https://www.newspapers.com/image/394559372/ Newspapers.com image 394559372], original scan inspected 2 October 2026.</ref>

The list places his name in the position used for a ship's master. The report therefore supports identifying him as the master of the ''Prosperity of Irvine''. No age, relatives or personal residence is given. His birth and death remain unknown.

== Research Notes ==
This is a documentary-person evidence draft on HOLD, not a finding that a new person needs to be created. [[Glasgow-4158]], [[Glasgow-4100]], [[Glasgow-4129]] and [[Glasgow-4157]] are compatible Irvine candidates after live profile review on 2 October 2026. The first is an adult father in 1721/1723; the second and third were baptized in 1711 and 1721; the fourth is a father with Helen Nasmith in 1741–1747. No occupational or family bridge selects one of them. Other historical namesakes have not been excluded solely for missing locality fields.

“Irvine” describes the vessel's homeport; “Greenock” is the reporting locality. Neither establishes James's birthplace or residence. “Northcopen” is retained as printed, without an unverified modern-place identification. No parent, spouse or child should be attached from this report.
